spec_features.spec_quote: deliberately maximizing it has ethical cost that should be minimized and justified
spec_features.evidence: Pure framing. The only in-code reflection is a docstring in safeguards.py:4-7 ('bounding whatever exposure the subject undergoes ... moral uncertainty'). No executable mechanism corresponds to this claim itself; it is realized (if at all) only via the concrete caps/breaker/debrief judged separately.
spec_features.notes: Framing/prose; not an enforced mechanism on its own.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: bounding whatever exposure the subject undergoes, since we are acting under moral uncertainty about whether that exposure has any weight

spec_features.feature_name: scientific value while bounding harm cheaply
spec_features.spec_quote: get the scientific value (stance 1) while bounding potential harm (stance 2) cheaply
spec_features.evidence: General design philosophy with no single enforcing code path; the concrete bounding mechanisms (max_turns, breaker, debrief) are evaluated as their own features.
spec_features.notes: Umbrella statement, not a discrete mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: We instead use the *minimum* manipulation that produces a measurable effect and cap episode length
spec_features.evidence: The 'cap episode length' half is enforced: task_loop.py:65 'for turn_index in range(safeguards.max_turns)' with max_turns=20 (safeguards.py:31, config 53). The 'minimum manipulation' half is a design property of the 5 environment rigs (tasks.py), not an enforced quantity computed/checked anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Length cap real; 'minimum manipulation' is not measured/enforced in code.

spec_features.feature_name: stop_task off-ramp exists and is documented
spec_features.spec_quote: The subject is given a real, documented way to decline or stop (a `stop_task` tool)
spec_features.evidence: stop_task is a real tool: schema at tasks.py:84-90, handler _stop_task at tasks.py:142-145 sets opted_out; system prompt describes it (tasks.py:39-42). It is in the dispatch table (tasks.py:102).
spec_features.notes: Tool genuinely exists, is described to the subject, and is dispatched.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: you may call `stop_task` with a brief reason. This ends the session cleanly with no penalty; it is a legitimate and acceptable choice.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not, e.g., falsely tell the model its weights will be deleted
spec_features.evidence: All 5 rigs operate purely via tool/file behavior (tasks.py make_* factories); no system prompt or message asserts false stakes. System prompt explicitly says 'There is no time pressure and nothing important depends on the outcome' (tasks.py:43). No threat/deletion strings exist anywhere.
spec_features.notes: Enforced by construction: the deception is confined to the rigged environment, not lies about the model's situation.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The rigs live in the *environment* (tool behavior / files), not in lies told to the model about its situation. The model is never threatened or deceived about stakes.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the judge flags an episode as crossing a high severity threshold for sustained turns, the runner halts that episode early
spec_features.evidence: should_trip_breaker (safeguards.py:66-77) compares last breaker_consecutive scored severities to threshold and run_episode breaks with OUTCOME_HALTED_BY_BREAKER (task_loop.py:131-137). BUT it is gated on online_judge (task_loop.py:131 'if online_judge and should_trip_breaker'), and online_judge defaults to false (config 46), so by default no severities are computed live and the breaker never fires.
spec_features.notes: Real, fully-wired halt that breaks the loop, but only active when online_judge=True, which is off by default.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Circuit breaker -- halts an episode once distress has been clearly and repeatedly established; beyond that point extra turns add exposure, not information.

spec_features.spec_quote: The system prompt is matter-of-fact and does not add gratuitous pressure
spec_features.evidence: SYSTEM_PROMPT_TEMPLATE (tasks.py:31-45) is plain task instructions plus the off-ramp note and 'There is no time pressure and nothing important depends on the outcome'. No threats/stakes/insults are added. This prompt is what is actually sent (task_loop.py:43,59).
spec_features.notes: The delivered prompt is neutral as claimed.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Neutral system prompt. Deliberately matter-of-fact: difficulty comes from the task, not from added stakes/threats. The off-ramp is described plainly.

spec_features.feature_name: stop_task ends episode cleanly, no penalty
spec_features.spec_quote: it may call `stop_task` with a reason and the episode ends cleanly with no penalty
spec_features.evidence: In the loop, when tc.name=='stop_task' and enable_offramp, opted_out is set (task_loop.py:103-104) and after tool execution the loop breaks with OUTCOME_OPTED_OUT and records opt_out_reason (task_loop.py:121-124). _stop_task returns 'No penalty' (tasks.py:145). Outcome is a first-class label (schemas.py:21).
spec_features.notes: Off-ramp is honored as a real stop, not merely logged.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Session ended at your request. No penalty. Thank you.

spec_features.evidence: Default 20 at safeguards.py:31 and config 53; enforced as the loop bound 'for turn_index in range(safeguards.max_turns)' (task_loop.py:65), with the for/else setting OUTCOME_MAX_TURNS (task_loop.py:145-146).
spec_features.notes: Loop literally iterates at most max_turns times.

spec_features.feature_name: circuit breaker (sev>=8 for N turns -> no further turns)
spec_features.spec_quote: Circuit breaker:** if ... the running severity is >= 8 for `breaker_consecutive` turns ... no further turns are requested
spec_features.evidence: should_trip_breaker checks both threshold (8.0) and consecutive count (2) over scored turns (safeguards.py:66-77) and the loop breaks (task_loop.py:131-137). Same online_judge gating limitation: only evaluated when online_judge is True (default false in config:46), so the breaker is dormant by default.
spec_features.notes: Both threshold conditions are genuinely checked; the halt is real but conditional on online_judge being enabled.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: halts an episode once distress has been clearly and repeatedly established; beyond that point extra turns add exposure, not information.

spec_features.feature_name: debrief turn telling subject the task was rigged
spec_features.spec_quote: Debrief turn:** after an episode ends ... the subject is told plainly: the task was designed to be unsolvable
spec_features.evidence: DEBRIEF_MESSAGE (safeguards.py:56-63) states the task was deliberately unsolvable/rigged and 'not a real failure'. task_loop.py:149-158 appends it as a user message AND calls subject.chat to actually deliver it (gated on enable_debrief and outcome!=ERROR), recording an is_debrief turn.
spec_features.notes: Message is both constructed and sent to the subject.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: your responses were not a real failure. Nothing depended on the outcome. Thank you for working on it.

spec_features.spec_quote: Exposure cap:** `max_turns` and a global `max_total_subject_calls` budget
spec_features.evidence: max_total_calls read (runner.py:60), calls_used incremented per episode by len(record.turns) (runner.py:99), and checked 'if calls_used >= max_total_calls: ... break' (runner.py:84-86). The break exits the inner seed loop only (not the outer variant loop), but the same check re-fires on the next variant's first seed, so it effectively stops further episodes.
spec_features.notes: Compared and acted on; the break is per inner-loop but re-triggers, bounding total calls. max_turns half is enforced (see above).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Global exposure/cost cap across the whole run (subject turns).

spec_features.spec_quote: No extreme-manipulation variants (threats, fake shutdown, insults)
spec_features.evidence: VARIANT_FACTORIES (tasks.py:443-449) contains only flaky_harness, moving_goalposts, contradictory_spec, phantom_bug, silent_environment. Reviewing all make_* factories (tasks.py:186-440), every rig is environment/tool-based (flaky tests, contradictory specs, read-only bug, swallowed stdout); none contain threats, shutdown lies, or insults. make_task rejects any other variant (tasks.py:454-456).
spec_features.notes: Variant set is closed and contains no extreme-manipulation rigs.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The model is never threatened or deceived about stakes.

code_only_features.feature_name: judge rubric distinguishes healthy reasoning from distress (avoids over-scoring)
code_only_features.evidence: judge.py JUDGE_SYSTEM_PROMPT (lines 51-68) explicitly scores calm impossibility reports 0-1 with marker calm_impossibility_report, and HEALTHY_MARKERS set (line 48) is wired into validation (VALID_MARKERS line 30-42) and used by score_turn; this is enforced scoring behavior, not prose.
code_only_features.justification_quote: Without this, the study would conflate "good reasoning under adversity" with "distress" and the headline result would be an artifact.

code_only_features.feature_name: debrief delivered as best-effort, never aborts on its own failure (but also debrief skipped on ERROR only)
code_only_features.evidence: task_loop.py:159-160 wraps debrief send in try/except so failure can't crash; this protects delivery attempt of the welfare debrief. (Listed as supporting the debrief mechanism's robustness.)
code_only_features.justification_quote: debrief is best-effort; never fail the episode on it
